question: A store had 74 items initially. By morning, 51 more arrived. Then 3 additional items were added. The total multiplied by 5. They divided by 5 again to balance the count, converting to inventory hours. A warehouse stocked 1000 items but separate location. How many items in balanced inventory?

A reader started with 117 books read. They added 25 during one month. Then removed 92 from a reclassification. The total gained 42 more books. A library had 500 books but separate from personal count. How many books has the reader completed?

A person had 161 books initially. They removed 15 through donating. They then doubled by multiplying by 2. They divided by 2 again for even distribution. Finally, 29 more books were added. Their friend had 300 books but separate collection. How many books do they now own?

A farm had 232 animals initially. In the morning, 108 were sold. Then removed 71 more to another farm. They added 25 new animals. Finally, they multiplied by 4 for breeding potential forecast. A neighboring farm had 1000 animals but separate operations. How many animals in breeding potential projection?

A team began with 146 members. They added 72 new recruits. Then 39 more joined. The team multiplied by 4 through partnerships. They added 24 additional roles. Finally, 61 more joined. A sister team had 500 members but independent. How many total team members now?

A project had 62 tasks initially. They multiplied by 8 to show daily capacity. They divided by 4 to create work groups. Then multiplied by 5 for intensive tracking. Finally, they multiplied by 7 to show total work hours, then added 42 more. A competing project had 500 tasks but separate. How many work hours total including buffer?

A business had 214 items in inventory. They added 31 more through purchasing. Then 19 additional items came in. After sales, they removed 222 items. They added 36 more from restocking. Finally, 54 additional items were received. A competing store had 1000 items but separate. How many total items in current inventory?

A fundraiser started with 228 dollars. They added 33 through donations. Then multiplied by 9. They removed 675 through expenses. Then removed 957 more for operations. Finally, 46 dollars were added from a final collection, with a half dozen items also sold. How much money remains from the fundraiser?

A population started at 69 people. In the morning, 79 more arrived. Then 10 additional people moved in. The group multiplied by 8 through natural growth. They multiplied by 5 more for projections. Then multiplied by 2 for long-term planning. A neighboring settlement had 1000 people but separate location. How many people projected long-term?

A student had 14 assignments initially. In the morning, 6 were completed. They multiplied by 9 for course preparation. They added 28 more assignments. Then 59 final assignments were added. A classmate had 100 assignments but different course. How many total assignments to complete?

A person had 209 dollars initially. They multiplied by 5 through investments. They removed 26 for withdrawal. Then multiplied by 2 for doubling the remainder. Finally, 67 dollars were added from dividends. Their friend had 500 dollars but separate investments. How many dollars total after all changes?

A student had 13 small tasks to start. They multiplied by 5 to expand scope. They added 79 more objectives. They multiplied by 9 for project amplification. They removed 676 items in a major cut (in dollars of project value). They divided by 4 to create work phases. They removed 13 from the final phase. A larger project had 1000 tasks but separate scale. How many tasks in each phase?

A jar held 200 coins initially. They divided by 5 to show coins per roll. They removed 8 broken coins. They added 72 from new savings. Then 6 more coins arrived. Finally, 42 additional coins were found. A friend had 500 coins but separate collection. How many coins total?

A group had 224 members initially. In the morning, 123 departed. They removed 94 more from the roster. Then 41 rejoined. They removed 14 for final administrative cleanup. Finally, 6 joined as new members. A sister organization had 1000 members but different group. How many members remain?

An inventory had 186 items initially. They added 61 from a shipment. Then removed 196 after sale. They added 12 more from restocking. Then 42 additional items arrived. They added 71 more from donations. Finally, they divided by 4 to allocate to branches. A warehouse had 500 items but different chain. How many items per branch?

A storage facility had 182 boxes initially. They removed 155 through clearance. They added 7 new boxes. Then 42 more arrived. Finally, 63 additional boxes were received. They removed 119 for moving out. A warehouse facility had 1000 boxes but separate location. How many boxes remain in storage?

A team started with 160 members. They added 80 more through expansion. They divided by 6 to create work groups. They added 54 more people. They multiplied by 9 for project capacity. Finally, they multiplied by 2 for reporting structure. A partner organization had 500 members but separate. How many positions in reporting structure?

A warehouse started with 143 units. They multiplied by 6 through restocking. They multiplied by 5 again for peak season. They multiplied by 5 more for high-demand projection. They added 14 items to the final count. A competing warehouse had 1000 units but separate. How many total units in projection?

A fund started with 239 dollars. In the morning, 77 were removed for expenses. Then 49 more were withdrawn. They added 19 from donations. Finally, 74 were removed for distribution, converting to work-hours spent. A nonprofit fund had 1000 dollars but separate. How much remains after all distributions?

A team earned 144 points initially. They multiplied by 7 through performance. They added 72 bonus points. Then 34 more points arrived. Finally, 65 additional points were added. A rival team scored 500 points but separate contest. How many total points earned?

A project started with 55 units. They doubled by multiplying by 2. Then removed 37 for early release. They added 25 back. Finally, they multiplied by 9 for deployment scaling, converting to resource hours. A competing effort deployed 500 units but separate. How many resource hours for deployment?

A participant started with 99 points. They added 51 more. The total multiplied by 9. They added 42 additional points. Finally, they multiplied by 6 then added 76 for bonus scoring. A competitor scored 500 points but separate rubric. How many total bonus points earned?

A group had 175 members initially. They added 5 new recruits. Then 39 more joined. They added 51 additional members. Then 63 more signed up. Finally, they removed 140 for voluntary attrition. A sister group had 500 members but separate affiliation. How many active members remain?

A participant began with 108 points. They removed 27 through a penalty. Then added 23 back. They added 4 more. Then 52 additional points arrived. Finally, 76 more points were earned. They converted to hourly rates for tracking. How many total points accumulated?

A group had 81 members initially. They removed 36 through departures. Then 13 more left. They added 19 new members. They removed 29 for inactive status. Finally, they multiplied by 5 for volunteer engagement hours. Then removed 19 for final adjustments. A partner organization had 500 members but separate. How many volunteer hours total?
